title: Stranger Things: The Night Will Vanished
description: A bad D&D roll, a bike that never makes it home, and a world flipped to its black side—Go Deep into November 6, 1983.

questions.question: On November 6, 1983, Will Byers vanishes on his bike ride home through what fictional Indiana town?
questions.hint: This Indiana town has some strange secrets
questions.explanation: The Duffers pitched the show as "Montauk." Winter shooting on Long Island was impractical, so Hawkins was built in Georgia.

questions.question: Hours before Will vanishes from Hawkins, the boys' ten-hour campaign ends when Will rolls a seven against which D&D monster?
questions.hint: He needed a 13 to fireball it
questions.explanation: "The Demogorgon. It got me," Will tells Mike. That same night, something with too many teeth answers the roll for real.

questions.question: After the Demogorgon takes Will, Joyce Byers strings up Christmas lights to talk across worlds. What does Will's first coded message say he is?
questions.explanation: A phone melts. Lights blink. Joyce paints the alphabet on the wall. When the bulbs finally speak, the comfort is also a horror: he never left.

questions.question: Will is "right here" in what parallel dimension Eleven opens—named when she flips the D&D board to its black side?
questions.explanation: Eleven names it in "The Flea and the Acrobat." Mr. Clarke's tightrope-walker analogy supplies the physics; the board supplies the poetry.

questions.question: Eleven opened that Upside Down as Dr. Brenner's test subject, but her mother, Terry Ives, gave her a real name first. What is it?
questions.hint: Four letters, as plain as a name gets
questions.explanation: Terry was tied to MKUltra lore in the show's mythos; Brenner took the baby. Hopper's forged papers finally make her Jane Hopper.

questions.question: What frozen breakfast is Eleven's favorite food?
What typeface family does the glowing red title evoke—borrowed from vintage Stephen King paperbacks?
questions.hint: Judge a show by its cover

easterEgg.title: Judge a show by its cover
easterEgg.text: That glowing red title is a modified ITC Benguiat. The Duffers sent the designers a stack of vintage Stephen King paperbacks and asked for the feeling of cracking one open.
